subject: CloudWave: subcontractor data residency + DPA redlines
messages:
From: Anna Szabo <anna.szabo@cloudwave.io>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Pavel Novotny <pavel@cloudwave-partners.com>, legal@cloudwave.io
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 18:12:00 +0200
Subject: Notice: addition of EU subcontractor + DPA clarifications

Hi Neha,

Quick heads-up from CloudWave procurement: we are engaging a small data routing partner in Prague (named DataPivot) to provide edge buffering for EU customers. Their work will involve transient KV caching and metadata necessary for regional performance optimization.

Two asks from our side so we can keep the deal timeline intact (target signature 4/22):
- Can Redwood confirm whether the current DPA covers this type of transient KV caching by downstream subprocessor? If not, what specific language do you require?
- DataPivot requires access to limited logs for troubleshooting. We need to know if we can provide them with a scoped access token (no customer PII by design).

Attached is a CSV export of the subproc details. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Szabo
Head of Procurement, CloudWave
anna.szabo@cloudwave.io
(Direct: +44 20 7946 0900)

Attachments: CloudWave_Subproc_List_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Anna Szabo <anna.szabo@cloudwave.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of EU subcontractor + DPA clarifications

Thanks Anna — and thanks for the file. Looping in Legal and Procurement.

Quick answers up front:
- We need to review DataPivot's role and the exact data elements they will touch. "Transient KV caching" is often OK under a narrow flow-down in the DPA but we typically require a subprocessor attestation and a confidentiality clause referencing our security controls.
- Scoped operational logs are usually permitted if redaction for PII is proven and there's an access control audit trail.

Marissa / Karthik: can you review the attached list and see whether there are any technical controls we must insist on (e.g., encryption-at-rest, HSM-backed keys, access logging retention)? If Legal is comfortable with a limited flow-down clause, Procurement can accept an annex; otherwise we'll need an explicit subprocessor addendum.

I'll propose a short MAM (mutual action) below to keep the 4/22 signature target.

Proposed next steps (short runbook):
1) Legal: redline DPA to add limited flow-down language + subprocessor attestation clause (48h).
2) Security: confirm minimum technical controls and any required evidence (48h).
3) CloudWave: obtain DataPivot attestation + sample config (72h).
4) Procurement: final sign-off on Order Form if (1-3) OK (by 4/20).

Would you be available for a 30-minute slot tomorrow 9-9:30am PT to align?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Accounts — Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

> Attachment: CloudWave_Subproc_List_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: legal-team@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA redline and minimum flow-down checklist

Neha / Karthik —

I reviewed CloudWave's subprocessor list and sketched an initial DPA redline (attached: Redwood_DPA_redline_20270412.docx). High level: we can accept a narrow EU caching subprocessor if the following are contractually required of DataPivot via flow-down or attestation:

- Purpose limitation: explicitly restrict processing to transient caching for performance; forbid analytics or customer profiling.
- Data minimization: specify exact metadata fields allowed (no customer PII, no content payloads).
- Encryption: encryption-at-rest for cached material using AES-256; keys managed by Redwood or KMS with documented separation.
- Access & logging: role-based access with 90-day audit log retention; access tokens rotated every 30 days.
- Subprocessor audit: right to request SOC2 Type II or equivalent, or a scoped security questionnaire and technical evidence (screenshots, configs).
- Breach notification: 24 hour initial notification to Redwood + preservation of logs for investigation.

If CloudWave cannot secure DataPivot's attestation within 72 hours, we should require DataPivot be bound under a direct subprocessor addendum to the DPA. I've flagged suggested contract text with [REQUIRED] markers.

Also, Procurement — see the attached OrderForm redline for small pricing adjustments related to EU egress.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_redline_20270412.docx, OrderForm_CW-DW-1043_redline.pdf

From: Anna Szabo <anna.szabo@cloudwave.io>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@cloudwave.io, pavel@cloudwave-partners.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:41:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redline and minimum flow-down checklist

Neha / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick review and the checklist. We can confirm the following from DataPivot:
- They only store encrypted metadata keys and transient buffer entries; no content payloads.
- They use AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit. Keys are KMS-managed (CloudWave can provide a write-only HSM-backed endpoint if needed).
- DataPivot is amenable to a scoped security questionnaire and can provide SOC-lite attestation (internal audit report).

Two items to flag for Redwood:
1) DataPivot's operational logs are retained for 120 days by default; they can produce a redaction workflow but prefer not to shorten retention.
2) They will need scoped access credentials from CloudWave; a token-based approach is the plan.

We can get the attestation and sample configs by end-of-day Thursday (4/15). If that works, can Redwood confirm whether the proposed [REQUIRED] clauses are acceptable or whether you need an addendum?

Anna

Attachments: DataPivot_attestation_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Anna Szabo <anna.szabo@cloudwave.io>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Redwood DPA redline and minimum flow-down checklist — security decision required

Markus — forwarding CloudWave thread and Marissa's redline. CloudWave says DataPivot can provide attestation and AES-256/KMS but retains logs 120 days (they request this as a non-negotiable).

We need Security sign-off on three specifics before I tell Procurement to proceed:
- Is 120-day log retention acceptable or do we require 90-day (Marissa suggested 90d)? Impact if we accept 120d?
- Do we require keys be managed by Redwood (preferred) or is a CloudWave write-only HSM endpoint OK from an exposure perspective?
- Any additional operational controls we must insist on for scoped access tokens (rotation policy, JIT access)?

If Security gives the green light today we can instruct CloudWave to obtain the DataPivot attestation and finalize the DPA annex. If not, we will require a direct subprocessor addendum.

Thanks,
Neha
